review_notes:
I read the whole target file (lines 1–118). It defines no simp lemmas or attributes. All of its simp uses are `simp only`/`simpa only` calls inside proofs. I checked the definition and API of `ModularConjugationData.rightAction` in ModularRightAction.lean, the `fixes_vector` field, `conjugationOperator_apply` in CommonRightAction.lean, and every use of `d.fixes_vector` across the KadisonKastler directory.

The one well-supported simp-interface problem is a missing rewrite lemma for `d.rightAction a Ω`. Because there is none, the same `change … ; rw [d.fixes_vector …]` unfolding is repeated in this file and in at least five other files. Two further files do it by unfolding the definition inside `simp only` (`simp only [rightAction, conjugationOperator_apply, …]`).

I do not recommend a global `@[simp]` attribute. `rightAction` is the preferred interface for most statements, and rewriting it everywhere could undo downstream statements written in terms of `rightAction`. A named lemma used in `simp only` / `rw` is the safe change.

Other `simp only` calls in the file (`heq` at lines 51–54 and `neg_zero` at line 56) use standard Mathlib lemmas and have no interface problem. I could not run Lean, so I have not compiled the proposed lemma or the rewritten proofs. The excerpts show that the lemma's proof would be exactly the existing `change`/`rw [d.fixes_vector]` steps.

findings.problem: Rewriting `d.rightAction (v n) Ω` to a form without `rightAction` takes two steps every time. You must first unfold the definition with `change` to `d.conjugation (star (v n).val (d.conjugation Ω))`, then rewrite with `d.fixes_vector`. The `rightAction` API in ModularRightAction.lean has `rightAction_mul`, `rightAction_one`, `rightAction_star` and others, but no evaluation lemma, either at a general vector or at the distinguished fixed vector Ω. So the identical local lemma `he` is restated in both theorems here (lines 39–42 and 75–78). The same unfolding appears in SpatialModularCoisometries, CenteredTestEnergy (`hr`), ModularProductTest and PositiveGraphAlgebraicApproximation. ModularScalingDefect and CoisometryShiftConvergence do it by unfolding the definition inside `simp only [rightAction, conjugationOperator_apply, …]`. That is the unwanted kind of expansion: it exposes `conjugationOperator` internals when only the value at Ω is needed.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two lemmas to ModularRightAction.lean, next to the existing `rightAction` API:

```lean
theorem rightAction_apply (a : Algebra M) (ξ : H) :
    d.rightAction a ξ = d.conjugation (star a.val (d.conjugation ξ)) := rfl

theorem rightAction_apply_vector (a : Algebra M) :
    d.rightAction a Ω = d.conjugation (star a.val Ω) := by
  rw [rightAction_apply, d.fixes_vector]
```

Do not tag them `@[simp]`, because `rightAction` is the user-facing form. Then replace both local `he` blocks in this file with `have he (n : ℕ) := (d.rightAction_apply_vector (v n)).trans (by rw [hd])`, or simply use `simpa only [d.rightAction_apply_vector, hd, Real.sqrt_sq ht.le] using hscale`. Callers that currently write `simp only [rightAction, conjugationOperator_apply, d.fixes_vector, …]` can use `simp only [d.rightAction_apply_vector, …]` instead.
findings.benefit: With these lemmas, Ω-evaluations of the right action have one named normal form, `d.conjugation (star a.val Ω)`. Proofs can reach it with `rw`/`simp only` instead of definitional `change` steps that depend on how `rightAction` and `conjugationOperator` are implemented. The duplicated `he` blocks in this file (and the copies in at least six sibling files) collapse to a single lemma reference. Changing the definition of `rightAction` would then mean fixing one lemma instead of every `change` site.

def rightAction (a : Algebra M) : H →L[ℂ] H :=
